blockers.quote: > HOLD: 4 s. Performed. You sit, lift a flat piece of cardboard from the recycling with piano keys drawn on it in pen, lay it on the table, shut your eyes and play. Every finger lands. A real piano sounds under the picture. Her spoon stops halfway. Her brows go up and stay up. You open your eyes for the applause.
blockers.why: Check #9, Earned stakes: she is present early, but the film gives the pair no warm shared beat before asking you to abandon forty years of friends for her.
blockers.fix: Replace with: "> HOLD: 4 s. Performed. You play the cardboard keys, eyes shut. Her spoon stops; then she taps the bowl in time. You miss a note, she catches the rhythm, and you find the ending together. She slides the last piece of toast to your side. You open your eyes, expecting applause."

blockers.quote: And within a week, it isn't just you.
blockers.why: Check #5, But / therefore: the boss's queue and the city montage currently join by elapsed time—an "and then"—rather than consequence.
blockers.fix: Replace with: "Your boss sells every coil before dawn. By the end of the week, the whole city is plugging in."

blockers.quote: She looks up. And she tells it.
blockers.why: Check #11, Never say the feeling: the narration repeats exactly what the performed shot already shows.
blockers.fix: Replace with: "For once, tomorrow gets nothing."

suggestions.quote: Two years in orbit bought one cosmonaut a forty-eighth of a second (c22). You bought a year with a pillow.
suggestions.fix: Cut the orbit insert and this line; move directly from the piano's personal gap to "But you'll fix the week."

suggestions.quote: The code. Four digits, last typed seven years ago. Your time.
suggestions.fix: Show several inside-town keypads with different codes flashing behind your hovering finger, so this particular memory loss feels caused rather than selected for the plot.

suggestions.quote: So, would you plug in? Tell us in the comments. And if you'd have done the same, hit like and subscribe.
suggestions.fix: Replace the spoken CTA with: "Would you plug in—or wait for two plugs? Tell us below." Leave like and subscribe to the end-card tags.

keep.quote: You were told you'd never run out of time in there. You did. Not hours. Hers.
They're queueing for a room that runs at her speed. You've got one. It's upstairs. It's free.
